stories.headline: Deep Agents keeps long-run context recoverable and inspectable
stories.read_scope: Complete conceptual guide: context rot, tool-result offloading, recoverable summarization, on-demand skills, subagent isolation, long-term Markdown memory, provider switching, middleware defaults and customization limits.
stories.summary: LangChain describes five Deep Agents mechanisms for limiting context rot: offload large inputs to files, summarize older turns, load skills only when relevant, isolate noisy work in subagents and persist selected knowledge as plain Markdown. Summaries remain recoverable, and user-controlled storage lets memory survive a model or provider change instead of remaining trapped in one service.
stories.why_it_matters: Keep active context small without deleting evidence. Store raw outputs behind previews, preserve summarized history for retrieval, separate exploratory work and review persistent memory edits. This makes long-running agents easier to audit, migrate and correct when their retained assumptions become stale.
stories.image_alt_intent: A long-running agent moves bulky tool output into files, condenses old turns, loads skills on demand and delegates noisy research, while a recoverable memory ledger remains under user control.

stories.headline: Build a permission-bounded release-note Agent Skill
stories.read_scope: Complete Agent Skills documentation: search paths, upward discovery, required frontmatter, naming and description rules, release-note example, tool exposure, manual selection, wildcard permissions, per-agent overrides and troubleshooting.
stories.summary: OpenCode documents portable SKILL.md discovery across project, global, Claude-compatible and agent-compatible paths. Its git-release example pairs strict frontmatter with bounded instructions for drafting release notes, proposing a version bump and returning a copyable command. Pattern permissions can allow, deny or require approval, while manual-only metadata prevents accidental automatic selection.
stories.why_it_matters: Create a read-only release skill, test its name and discovery, deny unrelated internal skills and require approval before any publishing command. Compare generated notes with merged pull requests, keep version choice human-owned and never let the procedure push tags automatically.
stories.image_alt_intent: A git-release SKILL.md with validated frontmatter feeds a read-only draft-and-compare workflow, while permission patterns block unrelated skills and a human approval gate prevents tag publication.
stories.agent_skills_evidence: Reusable read-only release-note procedure grounded in OpenCode’s October 17 Agent Skills documentation. Create `.opencode/skills/git-release/SKILL.md` with matching lowercase-hyphenated name, a precise description, manual-only metadata and instructions limited to drafting notes, proposing a version and returning a copyable command. Set unrelated `internal-*` skills to deny and the release skill to ask. Test discovery plus one repository fixture; compare notes with merged pull requests. Return DRAFT, REVIEW or STOP, never execute a tag, release or push. Require explicit human approval for any later publishing command.
